Title: Boulder City Council Study Session 8-24-23 (Community Broadband, Airport Community Conversation, Minimum Wage)

Topic1.Title: Community Broadband Update and Path Forward
Topic1.Summary: Staff presented research on internet access, resident survey results, and three potential paths for community broadband: a municipal internet utility, a public-private partnership, or a backbone lease and right-of-way agreement with a private provider. Financial modeling estimated about $218 million in build costs and a required average annual general fund subsidy of about $14 million. Council discussed concerns about cost, competition, shallow trenching impacts, and lease terms, and was generally leaning toward the backbone lease option.

Topic2.Title: Airport Community Conversation Update
Topic2.Summary: Staff presented the Boulder Municipal Airport community engagement process, including open houses, questionnaires, and a community working group that developed four long-term scenarios and near-term action items. Staff noted FAA grant assurances constrain closure options. Council asked about noise, leaded fuel, airspace, and whether further engagement should wait until new Council members take office.

Topic3.Title: Minimum Wage Regional Effort and Timeline
Topic3.Summary: Staff reviewed the regional minimum wage working group with Longmont, Louisville, Lafayette, and Erie, and Boulder County's decision to pursue a faster 2024 implementation. Staff explained the trade-offs of joining the county's timeline, including loss of collaboration and limited engagement. Council debated whether to move to a 2024 increase or hold to the 2025 timeline previously chosen, and ultimately gave a split direction to stay the course.
